title: Raise screening participation with reminders and accessible invitations
trigger: Low participation after checking invitation delivery and cohort composition
proposal: Audit invitations, provide appropriate language materials, and implement the screening reminder workflow
concrete_steps: Pull the non-attender list for the latest programme round from the screening register and break it down by language (Finnish, Swedish, other), age group and postcode area.
Audit invitation delivery (undeliverable letters, outdated addresses) so delivery failures are not counted as refusals.

Automate the reminder in the invitation system: breast, a reminder invitation 6 weeks after the first (breast manual §6.4); colorectal, a reminder letter with a free replacement kit if no sample arrives within 6 weeks (colorectal manual §10.5); cervical, a reminder 4–8 weeks after the first invitation (cervical manual §8.3).
Send invitations and reminders in the person's registered language using the Finnish Cancer Registry templates (Finnish, Swedish, English), and through suomi.fi where the person has enabled it.
For cervical screening, offer a pre-booked time and place and an HPV self-sampling kit to non-attenders after the reminder (cervical manual §8.4).
Write the reminder requirements into the screening service procurement contract (roadmap action 2.4.1).
target: {short} at or above the {comparator_name} rate ({comparator}; now {value}) in the next programme round; a reminder sent to 100% of eligible non-attenders
timeline: Reminder workflow live within 3 months; effect read from the next annual screening statistics (12–18 months)
first_90_days: Name the programme owner and pull the latest non-attender list
Audit undeliverable invitations and the invitation language
Switch on the automated reminder (6 weeks breast and colorectal, 4–8 weeks cervical)
Agree monthly participation reporting with the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5)
escalation: If participation stays below the rest-of-Finland rate after one round with reminders, commission an equity analysis by language and area and take it to the collaboration-area (YTA) screening steering group.

volume_rule.unit: invited people who did not attend
volume_rule.description: Invited (or picked) persons minus attenders in the latest programme year (d − n).

resource_rule.basis: Suomi.fi + postal reminder batch dispatch (incl. free replacement FIT kit on request) plus ~40 h one-time IT/procurement setup.

title: Close the loop after a positive FIT
trigger: Low recorded colonoscopy completion among positive tests
proposal: Audit screening-nurse contact and diagnostic follow-up, account for clinical exclusions and alternatives, then address verified workflow gaps
concrete_steps: List every FIT-positive person in the latest programme year without a recorded colonoscopy and reconcile each against endoscopy-unit and HILMO records (colonoscopies outside the programme count as completed follow-up).

Record a reason for every unresolved case: declined, clinically excluded, examined elsewhere, moved county after the positive test (the screening chain breaks on a move, colorectal manual §11.3), or lost to follow-up.
Make the screening nurse phone every positive person who has not made contact within about two weeks, as colorectal manual §11.2.1 requires.
Send completed colonoscopies to the screening register monthly (roadmap 2.4.5) so the loop closes visibly.
Record the date of the positive result and of the colonoscopy for every case and report the median and 90th-percentile interval quarterly.
target: Colonoscopy recorded for at least {comparator} of FIT positives ({comparator_name} rate; now {value}); a documented reason for every remaining case
timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; nurse call-back permanent; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
Reconcile against endoscopy and HILMO records and code a reason for each case
Start the two-week screening-nurse call-back
Agree monthly reporting of colonoscopy results to the screening register
escalation: If verified non-attendance persists after the call-back, review endoscopy capacity and travel distance with the collaboration-area endoscopy units and report to the YTA screening steering group.

volume_rule.unit: FIT positives without a recorded colonoscopy
volume_rule.description: Test positives minus attended colonoscopies in the latest programme year (d − n).

resource_rule.basis: ~20 min screening-nurse call-back & EHR reconciliation per unresolved FIT+ case, plus ~45 min specialist colonoscopy slot (~€420–€580 unit benchmark) for ~65% net unexamined cases.

title: Close the loop after a colposcopy referral
trigger: Low recorded colposcopy attendance among women referred from cervical screening
proposal: Track every referred woman to a colposcopy result: re-book non-attenders, make colposcopy units report to the screening organiser, then fix verified gaps
owner: County cervical screening and gynaecology leads
measure: colposcopy attended within the urgency window
referred women with no recorded colposcopy
colposcopy reports received by the screening organiser
concrete_steps: List women referred to colposcopy from programme screening without a recorded colposcopy and reconcile against gynaecology outpatient records.
Check each case against the urgency schedule in the cervical manual (Käypä hoito): HSIL or ASC-H within one month, AGC-NOS within two months, LSIL at the latest within six months.
Require colposcopy units to report to the screening organiser whether and when colposcopy was done and the colposcopic diagnosis (cervical manual §12.5).
Re-book non-attenders with a named contact person and a pre-booked appointment.
Report quarterly the share of referred women examined within the urgency window.
target: Colposcopy recorded for at least {comparator} of referred women ({comparator_name} rate; now {value}); every high-grade referral seen within one month
timeline: Reconciliation within 3 months; unit reporting agreed within 6 months; re-measure on the next annual statistics
first_90_days: Pull the list of referred women without a recorded colposcopy
Reconcile against gynaecology records and re-book non-attenders
Agree the §12.5 reporting fields with every colposcopy unit
escalation: If high-grade referrals are not seen within one month after reconciliation, escalate capacity to the collaboration-area gynaecology lead.

volume_rule.unit: referred women without a recorded colposcopy
volume_rule.description: Women referred to colposcopy minus women who attended colposcopy in the latest programme year (d − n).

resource_rule.basis: ~20 min gynaecology nurse reconciliation/re-booking per unresolved referral plus ~30 min colposcopy clinic slot (~€260–€380 unit benchmark) for net unexamined cases.

title: Verify lung treatment, stage and MDT records
trigger: Incomplete stage or MDT recording, or unexplained regional treatment-pattern differences
proposal: Conduct a joint clinical and coding review, standardise documentation and registry delivery, and monitor missingness before attributing differences to care quality
owner: County oncology lead and registry/data team
concrete_steps: Pull the county's lung cancer patients without any HILMO treatment record within 12 months of diagnosis and review each chart: treated in another county, treated but not coded, best supportive care decision, or died before treatment.
Check that MDT meetings are coded in HILMO with WZC15/WZC20 even when the patient is not present; the lung quality report notes that only direct patient contacts reach HILMO.
Audit the clinical cancer notification (kliininen syöpäilmoitus) to the Finnish Cancer Registry for the stage (TNM) field; nationally stage is missing for {stage_unknown} of lung cancers.
Automate the clinical notification from the oncology record (roadmap 3.2.1 targets 90% automated notifications by 2030 and 90% data coverage including stage).
For breast screening referrals with a missing outcome, send the final diagnosis back to the screening register.
Send corrected records to the registry and re-run this snapshot before judging treatment rates.
target: {short} back in line with the {comparator_name} rate ({comparator}; now {value}) after record reconciliation; stage recorded for at least 90% of new cases (roadmap 3.2.1)
timeline: Chart audit of the latest diagnosis year within 3 months; coding fixes within 6 months; notification automation by 2030
first_90_days: Pull the list of lung cancer patients without a treatment record for the latest diagnosis year
Reconcile against oncology, surgery, radiotherapy and palliative care records
Check WZC15/WZC20 coding of MDT meetings
Report corrected records to the Finnish Cancer Registry
escalation: If the share without a record stays above the rest-of-Finland rate after reconciliation, treat it as a care gap: start a clinical review of untreated patients (pathway_coordination playbook).

volume_rule.description: Adverse cases (patients without a treatment record; for MDT, patients without an MDT code; for breast, referrals with a missing outcome) divided by the years pooled (5 for 2019–2023). Uses the lung no-record count when the county publishes it.

resource_rule.capacity_unit: clinical chart & HILMO/FCR code audits / yr
resource_rule.basis: ~20–25 min oncology coder/nurse chart reconciliation + physician sign-off per unrecorded case, plus ~90 h one-time WZC15/WZC20 & automated clinical-notification EHR mapping.

evidence.label: Finnish Cancer Registry, lung cancer quality report 2019–2023 (MDT recording and missing stage)

title: Coordinate a fast-track lung cancer pathway
trigger: Curative lung treatment share clearly below the rest of Finland while treatment records are at least as complete as elsewhere
proposal: Pilot a pathway coordinator and standardised milestones from suspicion to treatment; review untreated patients with clinical teams and collect aggregate timestamp quality and interval measures
owner: Primary and specialist care pathway leads (pulmonology, thoracic surgery, oncology)
measure: share of patients reaching curative treatment
median and p90 interval from referral to treatment
eligible patients within the cancer-specific target
concrete_steps: Agree standardised referral criteria for suspected lung cancer with primary care and a direct GP route to chest CT without a separate specialist visit first (roadmap 2.5.2: standardised referral criteria and direct investigation routes); the clinical red-flag criteria are set by the county pulmonology lead.
Name a lung cancer pathway coordinator who tracks every suspected case from referral to treatment decision and books CT, bronchoscopy or biopsy, and MDT slots.
Discuss every new lung cancer at a weekly MDT before any non-curative decision, and code the meeting (WZC15) so it is visible in HILMO.

Collect four timestamps for each patient (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) and report the median and 90th-percentile intervals monthly; Swedish SVF milestones are an external model, not a Finnish target.
Review the county's patients who received symptomatic care only within 12 months for missed curative opportunities (stage, performance status, time to diagnosis).
target: Curative-treatment share at or above the {comparator_name} rate ({comparator}; now {value}); about {gap_per_year} more patients a year reaching curative treatment
timeline: Coordinator and referral criteria within 6 months; timestamps from month 3; curative share re-measured on the next registry quality report
first_90_days: Appoint the pathway coordinator and agree the referral criteria with primary care
Open a direct GP-to-chest-CT route for patients who meet the criteria
Start recording the four pathway timestamps for every new suspected case
Review symptomatic-care-only patients from the latest diagnosis year
escalation: If the curative share does not move within 12 months, take the case review to the regional cancer centre and the collaboration-area (YTA) thoracic oncology group (roadmap 3.2.3).

volume_rule.unit: patients a year short of the rest-of-Finland curative rate
volume_rule.description: (comparator − county share) × patients, divided by the years pooled (5).

resource_rule.capacity_unit: fast-track chest CT, biopsy & weekly MDT workups / yr
resource_rule.basis: 0.5–0.8 FTE thoracic pathway nurse coordinator (~€34k–€58k/yr) plus priority direct GP-to-chest-CT, bronchoscopy/biopsy and MDT slot ring-fencing per incremental patient.

evidence.label: National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 2.5.2 (standardised referral criteria, direct investigation routes)
National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.1.2 (cancer-specific pathways and target times)

title: Peer review of a survival or mortality gap
trigger: Survival below or mortality above the national comparator, outside the county interval
proposal: Run a structured peer review with a comparable county that has better outcomes: compare stage at diagnosis, diagnostic route and treatment mix, agree one pathway change, and re-measure annually
owner: County cancer centre lead with the collaboration-area (YTA) quality group
concrete_steps: Pick a peer county with a similar population profile and a better outcome for the same cancer (the snapshot lists demographic peers) and exchange aggregate pathway data.
Compare stage at diagnosis, the share with histological confirmation, the diagnostic route and the treatment mix for the cancer with the gap.
Check whether the gap is explained by incidence or risk factors (mortality reflects incidence as well as care) before attributing it to the pathway.
Agree one concrete pathway change with a named owner and record it with the YTA quality group.
Re-measure every year; national peer reviews are held once a year (roadmap 3.2.2), and persistent gaps go to the response mechanism in roadmap 3.2.3.
target: {short} moving toward the {comparator_name} value ({comparator}; now {value}) in the next annual Cancer in Finland release; one agreed pathway change implemented within 12 months
timeline: Peer review within 6 months; annual re-measurement
first_90_days: Choose the peer county and agree a data-exchange template
Pull stage, diagnostic route and treatment mix for the cancer with the gap
Schedule the joint review with both counties' clinical leads
escalation: If the gap persists for two consecutive annual releases, report it to the regional cancer centre under roadmap action 3.2.3 (response to peer-review findings).

volume_rule.unit: new diagnoses a year in scope

resource_rule.capacity_unit: annual YTA peer-review cohort cases analysed
resource_rule.basis: ~64 h/yr across oncology, surgery, pathology leads and registry analyst for structured demographic-peer benchmarking under Roadmap 3.2.2.

evidence.label: National cancer strategy implementation roadmap 2026–2031, action 3.2.2 (national peer development, annual reviews)

title: Maintain pathway performance and audit sub-county equity & timestamps
trigger: Headline county stages are in line or monitor-only, where sub-county language/rural equity gaps or missing pathway timestamps can still mask local delays
proposal: Audit sub-county screening attendance by language and municipality, pilot prospective referral-to-treatment timestamps, and share practices as a YTA benchmark peer
owner: County cancer-pathway quality lead and screening organiser
measure: screening attendance gap by language and postcode
prospective referral-to-treatment median and p90 days
concrete_steps: Stratify the county's latest breast, cervical and colorectal screening attendance by native language (Finnish, Swedish, other) and municipality so strong county averages do not mask pockets with 20+ pp lower uptake.

Verify that screening data are reported monthly to the Finnish Cancer Registry (roadmap 2.4.5) and that automated clinical notifications incl. TNM stage progress toward the 90% 2030 target (roadmap 3.2.1).

Start prospective recording of the four cancer-pathway timestamps (referral received, first specialist contact, diagnosis, treatment start) to close the national referral-delay data gap (roadmap 3.1.2).
Participate as a benchmark peer in the collaboration-area (YTA) annual quality review (roadmap 3.2.2) and watch any monitor-level indicators on the next registry release.
target: Keep {short} at or above the {comparator_name} benchmark ({comparator}; now {value}) while achieving ≥90% automated stage/clinical notifications by 2030 (roadmap 3.2.1)
timeline: Sub-county equity & timestamp check within 90 days; annual YTA benchmark review
first_90_days: Break down screening uptake by registered language (Finnish, Swedish, other) and municipality
Confirm monthly screening-register feeds (roadmap 2.4.5) and TNM stage notification coverage
Enable prospective 4-timestamp pathway logging for new lung, breast and colorectal referrals
escalation: If sub-county language or municipal screening gaps exceed 10 percentage points or any monitor indicator crosses outside the 95% CI, activate the stage-specific action playbook immediately.

volume_rule.unit: non-attenders or pathway records in annual equity watch
volume_rule.description: Latest annual non-attender count (d − n) or monitored cohort size for preventive sub-county equity auditing.

resource_rule.capacity_unit: quarterly sub-county equity & timestamp review cycles / yr
resource_rule.basis: ~36 h/yr of quality-lead and BI/registry analyst time (~€2.6k–€4.4k/yr) for quarterly sub-county equity disaggregation and timestamp monitoring.
